# Build: console-idle-load-fix (EMERGENCY)

Brett's words: "Yeah, that's no good. You need to fix that right now. Ram it through an emergency slot. That's no good." Earlier: "the console shouldn't be fucking using up a core and a half if it's fucking idle." and "We have it on lazy loading. It shouldn't be calling that much. It should only be fucking loading the plugins as needed."

## Problem (seen live on the VPS, Nov 23 2026)
- VPS load 10.7 with no build slots in use. The axf-console container sits at ~127% CPU while idle and has sent 72 GB out.
- `ps` shows short-lived `node` processes spawning every second inside the console.
- `docker logs axf-console`: on every console app load, ~30 status calls fire at once even though plugins are lazy-loaded: /api/control/{notify-control/state, claude-accounts/list, console-terminal/sessions-list, host-services/list (404), maintenance/status, glossary-index/stats, phone-connect/status, shipped-features/summary, ui-review/choices-settings, agent-slots/hard-limit, data-store/state, plan-studio-2/state, gate/rules-list, wake-listener/settings, build-orchestrator/priority-list}, plus /api/tracker, /api/plan, /api/pending, /api/build-queue. Each /api/control/<plugin>/... call makes a second HTTP request back into the same server (127.0.0.1:7090/api/plugins/...), doubling the work. /api/plugins/host-services is a 404 that is still called every load.

## Fix
1. Find where the console web app (apps/console-web) fires these on startup (toolbar badges, nav counts, settings preloads, control@1 state warm-up, etc.). Lazy loading must cover data too: a plugin's status/state calls run only when its screen, panel or a visible badge actually needs it. Nothing for an unopened plugin on load.
2. Make /api/control/... dispatch in-process to the plugin handler instead of an HTTP round trip to itself.
3. Find what spawns `node` per request (likely orchestrator status / plugin status endpoints shelling out to node); cache those answers (10-30 s) or keep one long-lived process. See the unlanded branch claude/console-orch-cache for prior art.
4. Drop or fix the host-services 404 call. Stop dead calls to retired screens (build manager, /api/build-queue, /api/pending, /api/tracker) if nothing visible needs them.
5. Check what keeps CPU up when no client is connected (background pollers, watchers, du scans) and throttle them.

## Done means
- Idle console (no screen open) under ~5% CPU; a fresh app load makes only the calls for what's on screen.
- Measure before/after (docker stats, count of requests per load) and put the numbers in the report.
- Tests green, commit and push as you go, PR, then land it. Short report in _claude/builds/reports/console-idle-load-fix.md.
